source.title: An Embodied Generalist Agent in 3D World
source.authors: Jiangyong Huang; Si-Long Yong; Xiaojian Ma; Xiongkun Linghu; Pu-Hao Li; Yan Wang; Qing Li; Song-Chun Zhu; Baoxiong Jia; Si-Yuan Huang

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present; no apparent cutoff or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling analysis to a multimodal embodied 3D agent’s instruction-tuning test loss and reports how it changes with training-data scale and LLM size.
record.gate_note: Section 4.5 reports LEO instruction-tuning test-loss curves as data scale grows, and comparisons across LLM sizes and alignment settings. These are results on instruction tuning in an embodied 3D setting, not held-out text-pretraining loss or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Citations to other scaling-law work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Section 4.5 tracks held-out instruction-tuning test loss of a multimodal 3D agent (LoRA-tuned LLMs) as tuning data grows, across three LLM sizes. This is a result on scaling in a fine-tuning, non-text setting (V5). It is weak evidence: the data range is 1.5–12×10^4, under one order of magnitude, and results are given only as a figure.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say LEO's instruction tuning 'conforms to the scaling law': test loss falls log-linearly with data, and larger LLMs and alignment help. The 7B-to-13B gap is small, which they read as possible saturation and a need to scale data with model capacity. In the conclusion they also say scaling data and model brings 'significant enhancements'. They fit no power law.
record.recipe_differences: Uses multimodal embodied 3D instruction-tuning test loss, varying data scale and LLM size; it does not reproduce text-pretraining loss or fixed-compute allocation measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Data scale, LLM size, and whether Vicuna-7B receives alignment change the reported loss or its comparison; the authors note possible saturation between aligned Vicuna-7B and Vicuna-13B.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The scaling evidence is reported as curves in Fig. 3 with qualitative descriptions, not numerical loss values or fitted exponents. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The test concerns instruction tuning in one embodied 3D agent setup, not the original text-pretraining or compute-optimal claims.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for other evaluations or ablations: they do not measure the scaling behavior named in the tested version. The text gives no additional numerical test-loss values beyond Fig. 3.

untested.parts: No power-law fit or exponent. No scaling over several orders of magnitude. No compute or parameter scaling within one model family. Image/video pretraining, repeated data and other transfer regimes are not tested.
No test of whether downstream scores are predictable from loss or follow a fitted trend. Only three LLM sizes from two families, under LoRA fine-tuning.

missing.what: Downstream task scores for LEO with OPT-1.3B, Vicuna-7B and Vicuna-13B. OPT-1.3B is clearly lower. Vicuna-7B and 13B are comparable and mixed across tasks.

record.verdict_notes: Scaling is a side analysis in an agent paper. The LLMs are frozen except for about 142M LoRA and encoder parameters. The model-size comparison mixes OPT and Vicuna families. 'Log-linear' on a linear loss axis is not the same functional form as a power law. The evidence for V5 is therefore qualitative and narrow in range.

versions.untested_parts: The study examines instruction-tuning test loss, not held-out pretraining loss; it does not test power-law loss in parameters, tokens, or compute under non-bottleneck conditions.
No small-run fits or predictions of substantially larger runs are reported.
No fixed-compute budget or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is tested.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
Tests instruction-tuning loss in this embodied 3D setting; does not test image/video models generally, repeated data, or other fine-tuning and transfer regimes.
The scaling analysis does not test whether downstream task performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
No exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted or compared across setups; no systematic curve bending or disagreement between published fits is tested.

rows.subject: LEO with OPT-1.3B (Aligned)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked instruction-tuning test loss as training-data scale grew.

conditions.value: growth shown in Fig. 3; x-axis marks 1.5, 3, 6, 12 (10^4)

rows.note: The authors state that all plotted curves decrease log-linearly with data scale; the plotted loss values are not given numerically in the text.
rows.check: Figure-only. Authors say the curve 'decrease[s] log-linearly'. The y-axis looks linear and the x-axis logarithmic, which describes loss linear in log data, not a fitted power law. The range spans only 8x. No exponents or fits are given.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V5. Decreasing test loss is reported, but the power-law form required by V5 is not established.
source_check.problem: Observed overstates evidence for V5: the authors describe log-linear loss decrease, without numerical curve values or a power-law fit.

rows.subject: LEO with Vicuna-7B (Scratch)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked instruction-tuning test loss as training-data scale grew, without the alignment stage.

conditions.value: growth shown in Fig. 3; x-axis marks 1.5, 3, 6, 12 (10^4)

rows.note: The authors state that all plotted curves decrease log-linearly with data scale; the plotted loss values are not given numerically in the text.
rows.check: Same caveats as R1: figure-only, log-linear rather than a fitted power law, 8x data range. Scratch versus Aligned is an alignment-stage ablation, not a scale variable.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V5. Scratch Vicuna-7B has decreasing test loss, but its power-law form is not established.
source_check.problem: The qualitative log-linear decrease does not establish the power-law form named by V5.

rows.subject: LEO with Vicuna-7B (Aligned)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked instruction-tuning test loss as training-data scale grew.

conditions.value: growth shown in Fig. 3; x-axis marks 1.5, 3, 6, 12 (10^4)

rows.note: The authors state that all plotted curves decrease log-linearly with data scale. They also report consistently lower loss than Scratch Vicuna-7B.
rows.check: Same caveats as R1: figure-only, log-linear rather than a fitted power law, 8x data range.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V5. Aligned Vicuna-7B has decreasing test loss and consistently lower loss than Scratch Vicuna-7B; no power-law form is established.
source_check.problem: Data-scaling improvement and alignment benefits do not establish V5's power-law form.

rows.subject: LEO with Vicuna-13B (Aligned)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked instruction-tuning test loss as training-data scale grew.

conditions.value: growth shown in Fig. 3; x-axis marks 1.5, 3, 6, 12 (10^4)

rows.note: The authors state that all plotted curves decrease log-linearly with data scale. They report improvement with increased LLM scale, but say the gap between aligned Vicuna-7B and Vicuna-13B is less significant and may indicate saturation.
rows.check: Data-scaling decrease is observed. The model-size gain from aligned Vicuna-7B to 13B is described as 'less significant', suggesting saturation. The size comparison also mixes model families (OPT-1.3B vs Vicuna), and only LoRA parameters are tuned.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V5. Aligned Vicuna-13B has decreasing test loss and consistently improves over aligned Vicuna-7B, with a smaller gap; no power-law form is established.
source_check.problem: Neither the qualitative data-scaling trend nor the smaller model-size gain establishes V5's power-law form.

relationships.condition: All four LEO settings (OPT-1.3B aligned; Vicuna-7B scratch/aligned; Vicuna-13B aligned), test loss vs tuning-data scale 1.5–12×10^4
relationships.reason: Authors report all test-loss curves decrease log-linearly with data (R1–R4). This is weak support: figure only, 8x range, no power-law fit.
relationships.display_finding: All four configurations showed log-linear test-loss decreases over an eightfold data range, without establishing a power-law form.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: All four LEO settings (OPT-1.3B aligned; Vicuna-7B scratch/aligned; Vicuna-13B aligned), test loss vs tuning-data scale 1.5–12×10^4
source_check.reason: R1–R4 establish qualitative loss decreases over an 8× data range. Section 4.5 describes log-linear decreases; Figure 3 supplies no numerical curve values or power-law fit establishing V5's required form.

relationships.condition: Model-size scaling, aligned Vicuna-7B vs Vicuna-13B
relationships.reason: The loss gain from 7B to 13B is 'less significant' than from 1.3B to 7B. Authors read this as potential saturation unless data is scaled too (R3, R4).
relationships.display_finding: The loss reduction from 7B to 13B was smaller than from 1.3B to 7B, suggesting potential saturation unless data also increased.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Model-size scaling, aligned Vicuna-7B vs Vicuna-13B
source_check.reason: Section 4.5 reports consistent improvement with a smaller 7B-to-13B gap and suggests potential saturation. Diminishing gains alone do not qualify or contradict a power law, whose form is not established by R3–R4.

relationships.condition: Downstream 3D tasks across LLM size (w/o Act setting, Table A.15)
relationships.reason: Based on the text; no row covers this. Vicuna-13B roughly matches or trails 7B on ScanNet tasks (Scan2Cap 65.2 vs 65.4; ScanQA 23.4 vs 24.3), but is higher on 3RQA (56.2 vs 51.9). Gains are not monotone with scale.
relationships.display_finding: Vicuna-13B scored 65.2 versus 65.4 on Scan2Cap and 23.4 versus 24.3 on ScanQA, but improved 3RQA to 56.2 from 51.9.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Downstream 3D tasks across LLM size (w/o Act setting, Table A.15)
source_check.reason: Table A.15 confirms mixed 7B-to-13B changes: Scan2Cap 65.4 to 65.2, ScanQA exact match 24.3 to 23.4, and 3RQA exact match 51.9 to 56.2. Section G.2 describes comparable performance and potential saturation; these results qualify consistent downstream improvement with scale.
